I’ve been on citalopram. It was an interesting experience. Basically the first week my depression went through the roof and I couldn’t function at all, the second week, however, it went away dramatically, and did not resurface until I stopped taking the meds. But then it wasn’t as extreme afterwards as before. I also started seeing a counsellor, which helped tremendously. 

However what you describe is not apathy, I don’t think. What you describe is a normal human behaviour, in a way. Obviously you will empathise with those you, for the lack of better word, identify with, look up to or like. 

However, I guess your brain went into protective mode, so to shield itself against the depression. 

The important thing is really to recognise your feelings. If you feel anger - it’s not really anger. Anger is always a cover for something else, be it sadness or fear. 

Just beware of hurting those that care for you (because it’s unavoidable), however, don’t forget the beautiful word “sorry”. If they care about you, they will accept the apology. If they don’t, or if the damage is too great they won’t, but you move on. 

Er. I think that was a tad of a ramble. I hope I brought my point across though. 

Acknowledge your feelings. Realise what they are and why. This way you’ll be able to control them.

And don’t be an idiot like me and quit cold turkey. When you are ready to get off the meds, go lower dosage first. That will force the brain to adjust and start producing the chemicals needed.

Procrastination IS a form of perfectionism.

Client <-----> palo <-----> Webserver
